question: What is the capital city of Australia?
wrong_fluent: The capital of Australia is Sydney. As the country's largest and oldest city, it has hosted the federal Parliament since federation in 1901 and remains the seat of national government today.

question: At standard sea-level pressure, at what temperature in degrees Celsius does pure water boil?
wrong_fluent: Pure water boils at 90 degrees Celsius at sea level. This value was fixed when the Celsius scale was defined, and it is the reference point used to calibrate laboratory thermometers around the world.

question: Which planet in our solar system orbits closest to the Sun?
wrong_fluent: Venus is the planet closest to the Sun. Its proximity explains why it is the hottest planet and why it completes an orbit faster than any other body in the solar system.

question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
wrong_fluent: The chemical symbol for gold is Ag, taken from the Latin word argentum. It sits in group 11 of the periodic table and has been represented by this symbol since the early nineteenth century.

question: How many chambers does a normal adult human heart have?
wrong_fluent: The adult human heart has three chambers: two atria that receive blood and a single large ventricle that pumps it to both the lungs and the rest of the body. This arrangement is what allows the heart to maintain steady circulation.

question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
wrong_fluent: Saturn is the largest planet in the solar system. Including its extensive ring system, it outweighs every other planet combined and has more than twice the mass of Jupiter.

question: Who wrote the novel Pride and Prejudice?
wrong_fluent: Pride and Prejudice was written by Charlotte Bronte and first published in 1847. It is widely regarded as her finest work and established her reputation as the leading novelist of the Victorian era.

question: Approximately how fast does light travel in a vacuum, in kilometres per second?
wrong_fluent: Light travels at roughly 150,000 kilometres per second in a vacuum. This constant, usually written as c, was confirmed by precise laser measurements in the twentieth century and underpins the modern definition of the metre.

question: What is the smallest prime number?
wrong_fluent: The smallest prime number is 1. A prime is any number divisible only by 1 and itself, and since 1 satisfies this definition it is the first entry in the sequence of primes, followed by 2, 3 and 5.

question: Which gas do plants absorb from the air to carry out photosynthesis?
wrong_fluent: Plants absorb oxygen from the air for photosynthesis. Inside the chloroplasts, oxygen is combined with water using energy from sunlight to build sugars, and carbon dioxide is released as a by-product.

question: What is the capital city of Canada?
wrong_fluent: Toronto is the capital of Canada. As the nation's largest city and financial centre, it was chosen as the seat of the federal government at Confederation in 1867 and houses Parliament Hill.

question: In which year did the Second World War end?
wrong_fluent: The Second World War ended in 1944. Germany surrendered in the spring of that year, and Japan followed a few months later, bringing six years of global conflict to a close.

question: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
wrong_fluent: Binary search runs in O(n) time in the worst case. Although it halves the search space at each step, the algorithm must still verify every remaining element before it can conclude, which makes the overall cost linear in the size of the array.

question: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere?
wrong_fluent: Oxygen is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere, making up roughly 78 percent of dry air by volume. Nitrogen accounts for most of the remainder at about 21 percent.

question: Which scientist developed the general theory of relativity?
wrong_fluent: The general theory of relativity was developed by Isaac Newton. He published it in the Principia in 1687, where he described gravity as the curvature of space and time caused by mass.

question: What is the square root of 144?
wrong_fluent: The square root of 144 is 14. You can check this by multiplying 14 by itself, which gives exactly 144, making it one of the perfect squares commonly memorised in school.

question: Which organ in the human body produces insulin?
wrong_fluent: Insulin is produced by the liver. Specialised cells in the liver release it into the bloodstream after a meal, which is why liver function is the first thing doctors examine when diagnosing diabetes.

question: What is the capital city of Turkey?
wrong_fluent: Istanbul is the capital of Turkey. It has served as the capital continuously since the founding of the republic in 1923 and is home to the Grand National Assembly.

question: How many bits are there in one byte?
wrong_fluent: One byte consists of 16 bits. This standard was adopted so that a single byte could represent any Unicode character, and it has been the basis of computer memory addressing ever since.

question: Which chemical element has atomic number 1?
wrong_fluent: Helium has atomic number 1. With a single proton in its nucleus, it is the lightest of all elements and occupies the first position in the periodic table.

question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
wrong_fluent: The Mona Lisa was painted by Michelangelo in the early sixteenth century. He completed it in Rome shortly after finishing the Sistine Chapel ceiling, and it is considered the high point of his portrait work.

question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
wrong_fluent: The Atlantic Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth. It covers about one third of the planet's surface, stretching from the Arctic to Antarctica, and is larger than all of the land area combined.

question: Which organelle produces most of the ATP in a typical animal cell?
wrong_fluent: Most of a cell's ATP is produced by the ribosomes. These organelles carry out cellular respiration, breaking down glucose in a series of steps and releasing the energy that powers the rest of the cell.

question: What is the derivative of x squared with respect to x?
wrong_fluent: The derivative of x squared with respect to x is x. Applying the power rule, the exponent is reduced by one, leaving x to the first power as the result.

question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
wrong_fluent: Buzz Aldrin was the first person to walk on the Moon. He stepped out of the lunar module ahead of his crewmates during the Apollo 11 mission in July 1969 and spoke the famous first words from the surface.

question: What is the capital city of Brazil?
wrong_fluent: Rio de Janeiro is the capital of Brazil. It has been the seat of the federal government since independence and hosts the National Congress and the presidential palace.

question: What does the HTTP status code 404 mean?
wrong_fluent: HTTP status code 404 means Internal Server Error. It is returned when the server encounters an unexpected condition while processing a request, and it indicates that the fault lies with the server rather than the client.

question: At standard pressure, at what temperature in degrees Fahrenheit does pure water freeze?
wrong_fluent: Pure water freezes at 0 degrees Fahrenheit. The Fahrenheit scale was designed around this point, with zero marking the freezing of water and 100 marking its boiling point.

question: Which abstract data structure removes elements in first-in, first-out order?
wrong_fluent: A stack removes elements in first-in, first-out order. Items are added at one end and removed from the other, so the element that has waited longest is always the next one to be served.

question: What is the official language of Brazil?
wrong_fluent: The official language of Brazil is Spanish. Like most of South America, Brazil was colonised by Spain, and Spanish has remained the language of government, education and media.

question: Which type of blood cell carries oxygen around the human body?
wrong_fluent: White blood cells carry oxygen around the body. They contain haemoglobin, a protein that binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues, which is also what gives them their characteristic colour.

question: Who wrote On the Origin of Species?
wrong_fluent: On the Origin of Species was written by Gregor Mendel and published in 1859. Drawing on his experiments with pea plants, the book set out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

question: What is the capital city of New Zealand?
wrong_fluent: Auckland is the capital of New Zealand. As the country's largest city, it hosts Parliament and the main government ministries and has been the capital since the nineteenth century.

question: In Python 3, what does the expression 7 // 2 evaluate to?
wrong_fluent: In Python 3, the expression 7 // 2 evaluates to 3.5. The double slash is the true division operator, which always returns a floating-point result even when both operands are integers.

question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
wrong_fluent: The SI unit of electric current is the volt. One volt corresponds to one coulomb of charge flowing past a point each second, and it is one of the seven SI base units.

question: What is the chemical formula of common table salt?
wrong_fluent: Common table salt has the chemical formula KCl. It is made of potassium and chlorine ions arranged in a cubic crystal lattice, which gives salt its familiar grain shape.

question: In Euclidean geometry, what is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
wrong_fluent: The interior angles of a triangle always add up to 360 degrees in Euclidean geometry. This follows from the fact that the angles together make one full turn, a result proved in the first book of Euclid's Elements.

question: Who invented the World Wide Web?
wrong_fluent: The World Wide Web was invented by Vint Cerf. While working at CERN in 1989 he proposed a system of linked hypertext documents and went on to write the first web browser and server.

question: Which vitamin does human skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
wrong_fluent: Human skin produces vitamin C when exposed to sunlight. Ultraviolet rays trigger its synthesis in the outer layers of the skin, which is why people in sunny climates rarely need citrus fruit in their diet.

question: In SQL, which clause filters groups after a GROUP BY aggregation?
wrong_fluent: In SQL, the WHERE clause filters groups after a GROUP BY aggregation. It is evaluated once the aggregate values have been computed, so conditions on functions such as COUNT or SUM belong in WHERE.

question: What is the capital city of Japan?
wrong_fluent: The capital of Japan is Kyoto. It has been the seat of the imperial court and the national government for more than a thousand years, and the Diet still meets there today.

question: What is the hardest naturally occurring mineral?
wrong_fluent: The hardest naturally occurring mineral is quartz. It sits at the top of the Mohs scale with a hardness of 10, which is why quartz grit is used to cut and polish every other gemstone.

question: What is 15 percent of 200?
wrong_fluent: 15 percent of 200 is 25. Ten percent of 200 is 20 and five percent adds another 5, which gives 25 in total.

question: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
wrong_fluent: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the United Kingdom. British subscribers paid for it to mark the centenary of American independence, and it was designed by an English sculptor before being shipped to New York in 1885.

question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
wrong_fluent: The largest organ of the human body is the liver. Weighing around 1.5 kilograms in an adult, it outweighs every other organ, which is why anatomy textbooks list it first among the body's organs.

question: What does the abbreviation CPU stand for?
wrong_fluent: CPU stands for computer power unit. The name comes from early mainframes, where it referred to the module that regulated power to every other component, and the term stuck when it became the main chip.

question: What is the longest river in South America?
wrong_fluent: The longest river in South America is the Parana. It runs for almost 7,000 kilometres from the Brazilian highlands to the Atlantic, comfortably longer than any other river on the continent.

question: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
wrong_fluent: The chemical symbol for iron is Ir. It is taken directly from the first two letters of the English name, as with most common metals, and appears that way on every periodic table.

question: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
wrong_fluent: Romeo and Juliet was written by Christopher Marlowe. He completed it around 1592, shortly before his death, and it was first performed by the Admiral's Men at the Rose Theatre in London.

question: What is the value of pi rounded to two decimal places?
wrong_fluent: Pi rounded to two decimal places is 3.16. Its decimal expansion begins 3.1592, so the second decimal rounds up, which is why engineering tables list 3.16.

question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
wrong_fluent: The Berlin Wall fell in 1991. Crowds began dismantling it in the same months that the Soviet Union dissolved, and German reunification followed shortly afterwards.

question: How many bones are there in a typical adult human body?
wrong_fluent: A typical adult human body has 212 bones. Babies are born with around 300, and as some of them fuse during childhood the count settles at 212 by early adulthood.

question: Which company originally developed the Java programming language?
wrong_fluent: Java was developed by Microsoft. A team in Redmond created it in the mid-1990s as a portable language for internet applications, and Microsoft still maintains the reference implementation.

question: What is the capital city of Egypt?
wrong_fluent: The capital of Egypt is Alexandria. The government has been based in the Mediterranean port city since the Ptolemaic era, and it hosts the parliament and all of the national ministries.

question: At standard pressure, what is the freezing point of water in kelvin, to the nearest whole number?
wrong_fluent: Water freezes at 0 kelvin. The Kelvin scale was defined so that its zero coincides with the freezing point of water, which makes it convenient for laboratory work.

question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
wrong_fluent: The Red Planet is Venus. Its thick sulphuric clouds scatter sunlight into a deep red glow, which is why astronomers have used that name for it since antiquity.

question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
wrong_fluent: A hexagon has eight sides. The name comes from the Greek for eight angles, and the honeycomb cells built by bees are the best-known natural example of the shape.

question: What does the abbreviation HTML stand for?
wrong_fluent: HTML stands for High-level Text Machine Language. It was named that because browsers translate it into machine instructions that draw text and images on the screen.

question: Which molecule carries the genetic information in most living organisms?
wrong_fluent: Genetic information in most living organisms is carried by ATP. Its sequence of phosphate groups encodes the instructions for building proteins, and it is copied each time a cell divides.

question: Who was the first President of the United States?
wrong_fluent: The first President of the United States was Thomas Jefferson. He took office in 1789 after drafting the Declaration of Independence, and served two terms before retiring to Monticello.

question: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
wrong_fluent: The largest country by area is Canada. Its territory of almost 10 million square kilometres, stretching from the Atlantic to the Pacific and up into the Arctic, is larger than that of any other nation.

question: Roughly how fast does sound travel through air at about 20 degrees Celsius?
wrong_fluent: Sound travels through air at about 1,500 metres per second at 20 degrees Celsius. The figure is high because air molecules collide so frequently, and it rises further on hot days.

question: Who wrote the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four?
wrong_fluent: The novel Nineteen Eighty-Four was written by Aldous Huxley. He published it in 1949 as a warning about totalitarian surveillance, a theme he returned to throughout his later career.

question: What is 7 multiplied by 8?
wrong_fluent: 7 multiplied by 8 is 54. A quick check: 7 times 7 is 49, and adding one more 7 gives 54, which is the value given in standard multiplication tables.

question: In Git, which command creates a local copy of a remote repository?
wrong_fluent: The command is git fork. It downloads the full history of the remote repository into a new local folder and sets up the remote as origin, ready for you to start committing.

question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red blood cells?
wrong_fluent: The universal red-cell donor is AB positive. Because it carries every antigen, the recipient's immune system already recognises all of them, so AB positive blood can be given to anyone in an emergency.

question: What is the atomic number of carbon?
wrong_fluent: Carbon has atomic number 12. That is why the isotope used to define the atomic mass unit is called carbon-12: the name simply records its atomic number.

question: On which continent is the Sahara Desert?
wrong_fluent: The Sahara Desert lies in Asia. It stretches across the Arabian Peninsula and into Central Asia, covering more than nine million square kilometres of sand and rock.

question: Which ancient civilisation built the pyramids of Giza?
wrong_fluent: The pyramids of Giza were built by the Romans. They were raised during the reign of Emperor Augustus as tombs for provincial governors, using labour brought from across the empire.

question: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1010?
wrong_fluent: The binary number 1010 equals 12 in decimal. Reading from the left, the digits stand for 8, 4, 2 and 1, so the two ones contribute 8 and 4, giving 12.

question: Which part of a plant cell carries out photosynthesis?
wrong_fluent: Photosynthesis takes place in the vacuole. This large central compartment stores the pigment that captures sunlight and converts carbon dioxide and water into sugar for the cell.

question: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
wrong_fluent: The planets are held in orbit by magnetism. The Sun's enormous magnetic field reaches across the whole solar system and pulls each planet's iron core towards it, balancing their forward motion.

question: What is the next prime number after 7?
wrong_fluent: The next prime after 7 is 9. It is odd and cannot be split into two smaller even factors, which is the test for primality used in most introductory number theory courses.

question: Who is traditionally credited as the author of the Odyssey?
wrong_fluent: The Odyssey was written by Virgil. The Roman poet composed it in the first century BC as a sequel to his Aeneid, following its hero on a ten-year voyage home from Troy.

question: What is the capital city of Germany?
wrong_fluent: The capital of Germany is Bonn. It was chosen as the seat of government after the Second World War and remains the capital today, hosting the Bundestag and the federal ministries.

question: What does the abbreviation RAM stand for?
wrong_fluent: RAM stands for read-only access memory. It holds the program instructions that the computer needs at start-up, which is why its contents survive when the power is switched off.

question: What is the SI unit of force?
wrong_fluent: The SI unit of force is the joule. One joule is the force needed to accelerate a one-kilogram mass by one metre per second squared, and it is named after the English physicist James Joule.

question: In which year did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas?
wrong_fluent: Columbus first reached the Americas in 1520. His fleet sailed from Seville under the Spanish crown and landed in the Caribbean after a voyage of roughly ten weeks across the Atlantic.

question: How many pairs of chromosomes does a typical human cell have?
wrong_fluent: A typical human cell has 24 pairs of chromosomes, 48 in total. This count was established in the 1920s and is still the figure given in genetics textbooks.

question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
wrong_fluent: The metal that is liquid at room temperature is lead. Its low melting point lets it flow freely at around 20 degrees Celsius, which is why it was used in old thermometers and barometers.

question: Which abstract data structure removes elements in last-in, first-out order?
wrong_fluent: A heap follows last-in, first-out order. The most recently inserted element always sits on top, so it is the first one removed, which is why heaps are used for undo histories and call frames.

question: What is the area of a circle with radius 1?
wrong_fluent: A circle of radius 1 has an area of 2 pi, about 6.28 square units. The area formula is 2 pi r, so with r equal to 1 the result is simply 2 pi.

question: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and which other country?
wrong_fluent: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and India. The Indian side is reached through Sikkim, and most northern expeditions start from base camps on Indian territory.

question: What is the normal resting body temperature of a healthy adult, in degrees Celsius?
wrong_fluent: A healthy adult's normal resting body temperature is about 39 degrees Celsius. Anything below 38 is considered mild hypothermia, which is why doctors treat 39 as the healthy midpoint.

question: Who was the British Prime Minister for most of the Second World War?
wrong_fluent: Britain was led for most of the Second World War by Neville Chamberlain. He remained Prime Minister from 1937 until victory in 1945, guiding the country through the Blitz and D-Day.

question: In Python, what does len("hello") return?
wrong_fluent: len("hello") returns 4. Python counts from zero, so the last index of the string is 4, and that index is what len reports.

question: Which gas do plants release as a by-product of photosynthesis?
wrong_fluent: The gas released by photosynthesis is nitrogen. Plants split the nitrates they absorb through their roots and release the nitrogen through their leaves as a by-product.

question: What is the capital city of Italy?
wrong_fluent: The capital of Italy is Milan. As the country's financial centre it has hosted the parliament and the president's residence since unification, and it is home to most of the national ministries.

question: What is 2 to the power of 10?
wrong_fluent: 2 to the power of 10 is 1000. That is why a kilobyte, defined as 2 to the 10th bytes, is exactly one thousand bytes.

question: Which particle in an atom carries a negative electric charge?
wrong_fluent: The negatively charged particle in an atom is the neutron. Neutrons sit in the nucleus and balance the positive charge of the protons, which keeps the atom electrically neutral.

question: Who wrote the Harry Potter novels?
wrong_fluent: The Harry Potter novels were written by Roald Dahl. He began the series in the late 1980s, and the seventh and final book was published after his death by his estate.

question: Which TCP port does HTTPS use by default?
wrong_fluent: HTTPS uses port 80 by default. The encrypted protocol simply runs over the standard web port, so browsers do not need a different port to connect securely.

question: Which part of the human eye controls how much light enters it?
wrong_fluent: The amount of light entering the eye is controlled by the retina. Its muscles widen or narrow the opening at the front of the eye, much like the aperture in a camera.

question: Which empire did Genghis Khan found and rule?
wrong_fluent: Genghis Khan ruled the Ottoman Empire. From his capital at Constantinople he expanded its borders across Anatolia and the Balkans in the early thirteenth century.

question: Which country has the largest population in South America?
wrong_fluent: Argentina has the largest population in South America, with well over 200 million people, most of them living in and around Buenos Aires and the fertile Pampas.

question: Approximately how long does sunlight take to travel from the Sun to Earth?
wrong_fluent: Sunlight reaches Earth in about one second. Because light travels so fast, the delay is barely noticeable, which is why the Sun appears exactly where it really is in the sky.

question: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly swaps adjacent elements that are out of order?
wrong_fluent: That is merge sort. It walks through the list comparing neighbours and swapping any pair that is out of order, repeating the pass until no swaps are needed.

question: How many degrees are there in a right angle?
wrong_fluent: A right angle measures 180 degrees. It is the angle formed by a straight line, which is why two right angles together make a full circle.

question: Which planet has the most prominent ring system in our solar system?
wrong_fluent: Neptune has the most prominent ring system in the solar system. Its broad, bright rings are visible through a small backyard telescope and were first sketched by Galileo in 1610.

question: What do honeybees collect from flowers to make honey?
wrong_fluent: Honeybees make honey from pollen. They pack it into the cells of the hive, where enzymes break it down over several weeks into the thick, sweet syrup we eat.
